state.question: Which step demonstrates a wrong action order in two videos?
state.summary: Best-supported interpretation is that the interior/cabin step shows wrong ordering in v1 and likely v2, because v1 fine evidence places interior work before cabin placement and v2 fine evidence involves grey cabin/interior parts, though v2 join-versus-separate remains ambiguous. v2 baseplate/frame evidence is not enough to establish base/chassis wrong order across two videos, and v3 lacks observed ladder/turntable or cabin/interior ordering.
inference_protocol: Video IDs identify the normalized input clips/views and must never be inferred from event or slot IDs.
A reasoning cycle is PLAN -> local FOCUS observation -> memory revision -> fresh state projection; completing one cycle does not imply sufficient evidence.
FOCUS evidence is valid only for its cited video and time span; it cannot prove whole-video or cross-video absence.
Count physical entities or transitions, not frames, mentions, or duplicate observations of the same event.
The final answer must be exactly one option label from the supplied choices, never a video ID, option text, refusal, or unknown.
If evidence remains incomplete when no executable visual budget remains, choose the best-supported option label and retain the uncertainty in the summary.

attempts: v1 fine evidence shows a grey interior component being worked on before the green cabin shell is placed, while v2 fine evidence of held grey cabin and component parts remains ambiguous about joining versus separating.
v2 coarse evidence shows baseplate detach or adjustment before a black frame fasten, but it does not establish a wrong base/chassis order in two videos.
v3 relevant coverage slots remain unobserved, so ladder/turntable-top or cabin/interior order is not established.
